description: Create an automation on a board: when something happens, do something. The most useful action here is http_request, which calls an external API and writes the answer back into columns, pair it with the "scheduled" trigger and the board keeps itself up to date (prices, exchange rates, shipment status, weather). Triggers: item_created, item_deleted, status_changed, column_value_changed, date_approaching, scheduled. Actions: http_request, send_notification, send_email, send_push, change_status, set_column_value, create_cross_board_item, send_webhook, recompute_related_rollup. The scheduled trigger takes a cron in triggerConfig, { cron, timezone }: cron is five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) and timezone is an IANA zone that defaults to Asia/Jerusalem, so { cron: "0 22 * * *" } is 22:00 Israel time all year, daylight saving included, with no conversion to UTC, and { cron: "0 8 * * 1", timezone: "Europe/London" } is Mondays at 08:00 in London. The server checks every minute and runs each occurrence once; an occurrence that is more than about two hours late (after an outage) is skipped, not run late. The older form { intervalHours, runAtHour } still works (intervalHours: at least this many hours between runs, default 24; runAtHour: 0-23, run only during that hour of the day in UTC, so 08:00 in Israel is runAtHour 5 in summer and 6 in winter); when cron is present the other two are not read. By default a scheduled run executes the actions once for every row of the board that passes conditions, so filter with conditions, and a board with more than 500 rows is skipped. To run the actions ONCE per occurrence with no row (a daily report, a nightly call to your own server), add perBoard: true to the same triggerConfig, e.g. { cron: "0 22 * * *", perBoard: true }. A perBoard run reads no rows, so an empty board runs too and the 500 row limit does not apply. It allows only send_email with fixed addresses in to (no columnEmailField, no attachments), http_request (no responseMapping, because that writes into a row, so the rule below that http_request needs a responseMapping is waived) and send_webhook. Any other action, any conditions, and perBoard on another trigger are refused with a message when you save it. In a perBoard run the placeholders {{column name}}, {{item.title}} and {{column.<id>}} resolve to an empty string, and these are filled: {{run.date}} (the day of the occurrence in the timezone, YYYY-MM-DD), {{run.occurrence}} (the exact time of the occurrence as ISO, identical on every retry, so a receiver can use it to ignore a repeat), {{run.timezone}}, {{run.automationId}} and {{run.boardId}}. send_webhook sends its usual JSON with itemId and item null and adds perBoard: true, automationId, occurrence and timezone. Worked example, one daily report at 22:00 Israel time with no duplicates: trigger "scheduled", triggerConfig { cron: "0 22 * * *", perBoard: true }, actions [{ type: "http_request", config: { url: "https://my-app.example.com/jobs/daily-report", method: "POST", body: { day: "{{run.date}}", runId: "{{run.automationId}}@{{run.occurrence}}" } } }]; the app server ignores a runId it has already handled, builds the report from its own data and sends it with POST /apps/<slug>/api/_email/send (described below). For a fixed message with no server, one { type: "send_email", config: { to: ["owner@example.com"], subject: "Daily report {{run.date}}", body: "..." } } does it. send_push sends a notification to the phones of app users through the app's own Firebase project (set up once per app: push_status; try it with send_test_push). Its config: { title, body, data, userIds, recipientsFromRelation, includeRowOwner, sound, badge, dataOnly }. title and body take {{column name}} placeholders, title defaults to the row title. Recipients are the union of: the row's owner under row-level security (includeRowOwner, default true; false leaves them out), userIds (fixed user ids, as in list_app_users), and recipientsFromRelation, a dotted path of column NAMES such as "Client.Coach.Coach user" that walks relation columns from this row and whose LAST segment must be a people column holding user ids (a single segment is a people column on this board); it does not resolve the user linked to a row by an invite or by phone, so without such a people column use userIds or the row owner. data is a flat object of strings the app reads to decide where to open (itemId and boardId are added). sound: "default" or the file name of a sound bundled in the app; badge: 0 to 99999, 0 clears; dataOnly: true shows nothing and delivers only data (no title, body, sound or badge; iOS may throttle or drop it). With no recipient the action is skipped, not failed. recompute_related_rollup keeps one column of a parent row equal to an aggregate of its child rows (a case's next action date from its open activities, an order total from its lines): put the automation on the CHILD board (triggers item_created, item_deleted and column_value_changed with no column named, which fires on any column change), config { relationColumnId (a relation column of the child board; targetRelation = its name works too), targetColumnId (a column of the parent board, which must be in the same project), aggregate: "min" | "max" | "count" | "sum", sourceColumnId (child column; not needed for count), where?: [{ field: "<child column id>", operator, value }] (AND, same operators as conditions, e.g. done not_equals "true"), whenEmpty?: number | null }. min and max take number, date or datetime columns and the target must be the same type; sum and count write to a number column. With no matching child the target is cleared (min, max) or set to 0 (count, sum) unless whenEmpty says otherwise. It writes through the normal path, so history and the parent board's own automations see the change, but it does not start another rollup. At most 5000 children per parent; more fails the run and writes nothing. Rows imported with board-import (new rows) and edits through the App API fire it; updating existing rows through board-import does not. Two more things every action list can use: a { type: "delay", config: { minutes | hours | days } } action pauses the run and resumes the actions after it later (reminders, follow-ups); and any network action (http_request, send_webhook, send_email, send_whatsapp) may carry config.retry: { attempts (1-5), delaySeconds (1-60) }. send_webhook accepts config.secret for an HMAC signature. send_email sends mail from the organization to the people on a row. Its config: { to, subject, body, columnEmailField, fromName, replyTo, kind, attachments }. kind is "transactional" (the default: orders, receipts, notifications) or "marketing" (promotional mail: it needs the Pro plan or higher and a verified sender domain, and it gets an unsubscribe footer; people who unsubscribed are skipped). attachments is an array of FILE column ids on the triggering row (or {{column.<id>}}): the stored files in those cells are attached, up to 5MB in total, and a missing file is skipped instead of failing the action. Email is counted per month by plan: Free 300, Plus 3000, Pro 20000 (read the numbers with get_email_usage); a message held back by the quota is recorded as skipped in the communications log and can be resent from there. To send email from an app's own server instead of an automation, POST /apps/<slug>/api/_email/send with the app server key (X-API-Key, never a user token; the key needs the "email" or "write" scope, see create_app_api_key): { to: [up to 50 addresses], subject, html or text, replyTo, kind, attachmentIds: [stored file ids] }; each app may send 500 a day (429 APP_EMAIL_DAILY_LIMIT). create_cross_board_item copies a new row to another board: config { targetBoardId, title?: "{{item.title}}", columnValues: { "<column id on the TARGET board>": "{{<column NAME on this board>}}" } }; there is no mapping field, and a column left out is not copied. http_request fills {{column name}}, {{item.title}} and {{column.<id>}} placeholders in url and in body from the triggering row (lookup, rollup and formula columns included). body is an object (every string in it is filled and stays a string) or a JSON string, where a value inside quotes is escaped in place and a placeholder written outside quotes, as in "UnitPrice":{{Amount}}, goes in as a number when the value is a number, null when it is empty and a quoted string otherwise. A JSON body that does not parse after filling is not sent and the run fails; a placeholder with an unknown name is left as written and listed in the run log (unresolvedPlaceholders). set_column_value: config { columnId, value }; a string value takes the same placeholders, e.g. "https://track.example/{{Tracking number}}". It writes nothing (the run log says why) when a placeholder is unknown, when the value is one placeholder whose source is empty, or when the result is not a number for a number, currency, rating or duration column. To total child rows by a price that comes from a lookup or a formula, copy it into a number column of the child row with set_column_value and then run recompute_related_rollup on that column, both actions in one automation in that order. To act only on some rows pass conditions, e.g. [{ field: "<column id on this board>", operator: "equals", value: "New seller" }]. Change an automation later with update_automation; call list_automations first so you do not add a second one that does the same thing.

actions.description: e.g. [{ type: "http_request", config: { url: "https://api.frankfurter.app/latest?from=USD&to=ILS", method: "GET", responseMapping: [{ path: "rates.ILS", columnId: "<column id from get_board_schema>" }] } }]

config.description: Action-specific config, e.g. { url, method, headers, responseMapping } for http_request, { title, body, recipientsFromRelation, includeRowOwner, userIds, data, sound, badge, dataOnly } for send_push, or { to, subject, body, kind: "transactional" | "marketing", attachments: ["<file column id>"] } for send_email. A digest mail on a "scheduled" trigger (one run per row, not perBoard) can list rows of ANOTHER board of the same project that belong to that row: send_email config.relatedRows: [{ key: "late" (letters, digits, _), boardId, match: { columnId: "<column on that board>", to: "item" (a relation column on that board pointing to this board) | "<column id on this board>" (equal values: text and email case-insensitive, phone by digits, people by user id) }, conditions?: [{ field, operator, value }] (the automation condition grammar, AND), dateWindow?: { columnId: "dueDate" | "<date column>", from?: "today-7", to?: "today+3" } (days relative to today, inclusive; overdue = { to: "today-1" }), columns?: [up to 8 column ids or status, priority, dueDate, assignedTo, tags; the title is always first], sort?: { columnId, direction?: "asc" | "desc" }, limit?: 1..200 (default 50), emptyText?, moreText?: "ועוד {n} נוספים" }] (1 to 5 blocks), and skipIfAllEmpty?: true (send nothing when every block is empty). In body {{rows:<key>}} is the table and {{count:<key>}} the number of rows; in subject only {{count:<key>}}; every block must be used. The server refuses another project or organization, unknown keys, sealed columns, and more than 5000 candidate rows per block (the run fails, never a silent cut).

type.description: Action type: http_request, send_notification, send_email, send_push, change_status, set_column_value, create_cross_board_item, send_webhook, send_whatsapp, delay

conditions.description: Run only for rows that match, e.g. [{ field: "<column id>", operator: "equals", value: "New seller" }]

field.description: A column id on this board (from get_board_schema), or status, priority, title

operator.description: equals, not_equals, contains, not_contains, is_empty, is_not_empty, greater_than, less_than

trigger.description: Event that starts the automation: item_created, status_changed, column_value_changed, date_approaching, or scheduled (a cron with a time zone, or the older interval in hours and an optional hour of the day in UTC; see triggerConfig)

triggerConfig.description: For scheduled: { cron: "<5 fields>", timezone?: IANA zone (default Asia/Jerusalem), perBoard?: true }, e.g. { cron: "0 22 * * *" } for every day at 22:00 Israel time all year, or { cron: "*/15 * * * *" } for every 15 minutes. perBoard: true runs the actions once per occurrence with no row instead of once per row (only send_email to fixed addresses, http_request without responseMapping, and send_webhook; no conditions), see the tool description. The older form is { intervalHours?: number (default 24), runAtHour?: 0-23 in UTC }, e.g. { intervalHours: 1 } for every hour, or { runAtHour: 5, intervalHours: 23 } for once a day at 05:00 UTC; with runAtHour use 23, not 24, so a run that finished a little late the day before does not push this one out of its hour. When cron is present intervalHours and runAtHour are not read. For column_value_changed: { columnName }
